correctness.rationale: Domain: all 16383 nonzero binary plane quintic forms vanishing at the seven F_2-rational points; geometric smoothness, not mere F_{2^m}-point smoothness, is required. The 14-dimensional evaluation kernel and PGL_3(F_2) generators define a complete finite enumeration. The included inspected script generates all forms, partitions the group orbits, and uses the unit ideal of all three partial derivatives on each projective chart to exclude singularities over the algebraic closure; this gives 1512 smooth equations in ten orbits (eight size 168 and two size 84). For each representative the six Cech H^1(O_C) Frobenius coefficients define a 6x6 Hasse-Witt matrix, a=6-rank H and f_2=rank(H^6). An independently written GF(2) row-reduction/power check matched all ten displayed (f_2,a) pairs, namely orbit distributions (2,3):1, (2,1):2, (5,1):2, (6,0):5, giving equation-weighted 168,252,336,756. The ten six-tuples (c_1,...,c_6) in the frozen RESULT are distinct and the functional equation determines the degree-12 Weil numerators, so distinct F_2-Jacobian isogeny classes follow from Tate. I read the complete enumeration, field arithmetic and orbit code rather than accepting CERTIFIED as proof. The independent rank test checks representatives, not the completeness of orbit/smoothness enumeration; that completeness rests on a transparent exact finite algorithm with exhaustive loops and unit-ideal criterion, not on an extension-degree cutoff. No geometric-isomorphism classification or Newton polygons are inferred.
residual_risks: Completeness of a computer-assisted finite classification depends on correct implementation of the inspected symbolic Gröbner and orbit routines; independent rank checks alone do not redo the entire 16383-form census.
The isogeny classification is over F_2, not geometric curve isomorphism or a general genus-six result.

evidence: Existing geometric family counts do not give any genus-six Cartier ranks or Frobenius characteristic polynomial.
The general cohomological Cartier-Manin coefficient theorem is a method, not a computed family spectrum.
